title: I tried making and publishing a tiny game with AI in one evening
author: okiamvegan
selftext:
I wanted to see how far I could get without opening a game engine or setting up hosting. The first version took about two hours. It was technically playable, but the AI made the difficulty curve completely ridiculous, so I spent another hour fixing the spawning logic and adding a restart loop.

I published the result through PlayGama MCP because I’m experimenting with the product and wanted to test the whole “prompt → playable link → actual players” workflow.

The game is very small, but the interesting part was going from an idea to something other people could open almost immediately.   
  
What would you improve first: controls, progression, or visual feedback? Happy to share the game and the prompts if anyone wants to test it.   
  
Sorry for AI-ish style of writing, English is not my native language, but I hope it's okay too.

comments.author: BrownaroStudios
comments.body:
This sounds good in theory but I think it might hurt more than it helps.  My main concern with doing this is losing users who would have otherwise played the game if we had tested it and possibly losing them as users across our entire portfolio!  

I think if you were to do this though you'd have to focus entirely on the core gameplay loop and experience.  The UI could get polished later and update it with conveniences for users as you eventually do play the game more and generate a wish list.
